newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia inter-island truck traffic normal again.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia inter-island truck traffic normal again.

text.p: Indonesian inter-island truck traffic across the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra has returned to normal after bad weather caused a backlog of thousands of vehicles, port officials said on Monday.

Transport department officials on the weekend estimated up to 3,000 trucks were backed up at the Merak port in West Java and Bandar Lampung on the Sumatra side of the 40 km (25 mile) wide strait after bad weather interrupted services last week.

Rough seas decreased the frequency of services as passenger traffic increased ahead of the Christmas and New Year holiday period. Passenger vehicles get priority on the popular route linking Indonesia's two most populous islands.

However, officials said the backlog had been cleared by Monday after the privately-owned KM Utari, a roll-on roll-off ship with a capacity of about 250 trucks., began special services on the route on Sunday after the government chartered it to solve the problem.

"The situation with trucks has returned to normal after we started using the KM Utari yesterday," Suryabadi, the duty officer at the co-ordinating post at Merak port, told Reuters by telephone. Port officials in Bandar Lampung said the situation on the western side of the strait had also returned to normal.
